findings.detail: The idle empty cleanup submission also runs when canvases are open, not only with no canvas: one extra Submit per release round and process_events() returns true until it retires. Correct and harmless; the claims should describe it as event-boundary cleanup whenever no Ticket is outstanding.
No GIL release anywhere in the bindings and no Python references in the runtime, so a finalizer calling retire_objects cannot re-enter or deadlock on eng.mu; helper-thread GC stays serialized.

Failure before Submit removes the Ticket and retries later; failure registering the completion callback after Submit keeps the Ticket and poll() retries only registration; no duplicate successful Submit.
Delete ordering, live-peer queues, version gating and failure-path retirement are consistent; no double erase or lost delete found.
'raise error from retirement_error' replaces any existing __cause__ on the original error. Diagnostics only; not blocking.

The reader accepts exactly one more original-capture workflow hash (706a9d26); unknown or mutated revisions, including a candidate14 selector, are still rejected; the current workflow d5f9 is pinned only as required-CI policy.
Adding reviews and resealing changes only the candidate file hash and the provenance pointers; the scope digest, map bindings and both reuse digests are unaffected. Not circular.

The dated preparation14 'gap closed' checkpoint is historical and superseded by later 'no transfer' text; the 891 inventory counts 144 owned files against 145 because of its own wrapper. The final freeze must use the exact 145 plus the allowed additions.
All six dispositions are conservative; no added doc text found that promotes a finite or historical proof to release qualification (diff partially read).
